done_when: forge upgrade counts a run as in progress only while its recorded process is still alive (the same process identity the lanes use), so a run whose process is gone no longer blocks the upgrade; a live run still blocks it; new and existing repos get it

known.title: Not done: live CI waits do not block forge upgrade

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. Case: normal use - a close has a clean review and is waiting for the already-pushed code's CI before pushing its review record. `src/forge/close.py:438` enters `checks.after_code_ci`, but the `let_finish` wait at `src/forge/checks.py:123` writes no run-start record. The review lane has already ended, so the new scan at `src/forge/upgrade.py:101` cannot see the live close and upgrade can install a replacement release while it waits. The new test waits for a CI run-start at `tests/test_upgrade_waits_for_live_commands.py:34`, so it exercises the later recorded wait rather than this one.
findings.title: Not done: live CI waits do not block forge upgrade

stop.reason: Owner chose one more round on 20 Nov 2026: a live CI wait must block upgrade

why: forge upgrade refuses with 'Forge runs are still in progress' for runs whose process is gone: an intake read that joined its lane but never recorded an end, and a close review killed seconds after it started (lane left with end_known false); a client hit it on 20 Nov 2026 upgrading to v1.2.44 with no forge process running and had to install by hand
